_comment: Providers the gateway serves, in fallback order for model "auto". Golden rule: free. No provider may cost money or need a card; a free API key is allowed (tier K), kept in <state dir>/keys.json or the entry's key_env variable, never in this file. A copy at <state dir>/providers.json (default ~/.ai-gateway/providers.json) replaces this built-in list, so a broken provider is a config edit, not a rebuild. kind openai: an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint (url, optional models_url and model_filter, optional key_env). kind cli: a vendor CLI run headless (bin, ask_args with {prompt}, optional model_args with {model}, optional strip regexes removed from its output). kind tty: an interactive terminal app with no prompt flag, driven through a pseudo-terminal (bin, args; see the tty fields in internal/provider/provider.go). default_model empty = the first model the provider lists. min_interval_seconds spaces calls out; daily_limit 0 = no cap known. Every cli and tty run gets its own empty scratch directory (deleted afterwards), the entry's env, and the top-level preamble before the prompt (an entry's own preamble overrides it); cleanup lists what the tool leaves elsewhere per run. disabled: true keeps an entry in the file without serving it.
preamble: You are answering a question for another program, which reads only your reply. Do not create, edit or run any files, and do not look for a project: there is none. Put everything asked for, including complete code, in the reply itself.

providers.note: Only opencode's own free hosted models are listed. A model is always passed, because opencode's default on betelgeuse is the local bill-the-cat. Its google/* models use an API key, so the golden rule excludes them.

Freebuff has no prompt flag, so it is driven through a pseudo-terminal. The screen tells when the reply is finished (freebuff 0.2.36 layout: the typed prompt ends with a copy mark, and a finished reply is followed by a line with the copy mark and its duration). The reply itself is read from the conversation file freebuff saves, which is then deleted; the screen is the fallback, and there a reply longer than the screen is an error, not cut short. Freebuff's own banner says it may use data for AI training.
Off: Qwen Code's sign-in (seen on betelgeuse, Nov 2026) offers only a paid Qwen subscription, API-key providers, or a custom local server. No free keyless option, so the golden rule excludes it.

Answers on betelgeuse. strip removes the notice Copilot prints before its answer saying which model it chose. The token variables are blanked so Copilot uses its own /login session: on betelgeuse it picked up a personal access token from the environment, which lacks the Copilot Requests permission.

Off: on betelgeuse `amp -x` answers Out of Credits. Amp's own announcement says execute mode uses paid credits only; its free mode, if it still exists, is interactive only (/mode free) and would need a tty entry.
--trust skips the workspace-trust prompt in print mode (it stopped the first try on betelgeuse). Answers on betelgeuse.

The Qwen2.5-Coder-7B on rigel, behind Loadout: local, no quota, 32K context. The first call after another rigel model was in use pays a model swap. Endpoint taken from Bill's ModelBackend.swift; not yet called from the gateway.
Kilo's gateway: free models need no key, about 200 requests an hour per IP. From a public list of free APIs (Nov 2026); not yet called.
OVHcloud AI Endpoints, anonymous: 2 requests a minute per model, and reported as often rate-limited. Not yet called.
Free key, no card: 30 requests a minute, 1,000 a day. Not yet called.
Free key from Google AI Studio, no card; limits unpublished. Separate from the Gemini CLI's allowance. Not yet called.
Free key: only models ending :free are used, 50 requests a day. Not yet called.
Free key with NVIDIA Developer Program membership; limits unpublished. Not yet called.
Free trial key: 1,000 calls a month, non-commercial use only. Model ids from memory. Not yet called.
Free key for the flash model, one request at a time. Not yet called.
